items: `identifier` field — a persistent unique ID used to track an asset across renames/migrations. Added to `properties` (right after `name`) and to `required`.
`downloads` property added to `reuseFrequency.properties`, alongside the existing `forks` and `clones`.
`$id` updated to `https://gsa-share-it.github.io/code-json-schema.json` (reflecting the repository's move from the `DSACMS` org to `GSA-SHARE-IT`).
`permissions.usageType`
enum: M-16-21 exemptions are removed from the schema: `exemptByIPRestriction`, `exemptByAgencySystem`, `exemptByAgencyMission`, `exemptByCIO`, and `exemptByPolicyDate`

enum: `exemptByDisposableCode`, `exemptByExperimentalCode`, and `exemptByCommercialSoftware` are added, reflecting the SHARE IT Act's exclusions for exploratory/disposable code and commercial/COTS software.
`identifier` added to `required`.
`AIUseCaseID`, `SBOM`, `date`, `description`, `laborHours`, `languages`, `tags`, and `vcs` removed from `required` (now optional).
`feedbackMechanism` (singular)

`version`, `homepageURL`, `downloadURL`, `disclaimerURL`, `disclaimerText`, `relatedCode`, `reusedCode`, `partners` added as optional fields, taken from original [M-16-21 code.json schema](https://github.com/GSA/code-gov-data/tree/master/schemas)
`AIUseCaseID` added for assisting with agency collection of their AI Use Case Inventory as part of M-25-21 compliance
`SBOM` added to include software's SBOM in metadata as part of EO 14028

`categories`, `feedbackMechanisms` (plural, replaced by singular `feedbackMechanism`), `localisation`, `longDescription`, `platforms`, `softwareType` — these agency-extension-style fields were dropped from the generic gov-wide schema.
Migrated `$schema` dialect from `draft-04` to `2020-12` and introduced a formal `$id` (`https://dsacms.github.io/code-json-schema.json`).

Corrected the same structural bug present in `gov-schema-1.0.0.json`, where all field definitions were incorrectly nested one level too deep under a top-level `items` key instead of directly under `properties`.
`permissions.usageType` changed from a single `string` value to an `array` of strings, allowing multiple exemption reasons to be declared simultaneously.

Expanded and refined the exemption enum taxonomy: the old `exemptByLaw` was split into `exemptByNationalSecurity`, `exemptByNationalIntelligence`, `exemptByFOIA`, `exemptByEAR`, `exemptByITAR`, `exemptByTSA`, and `exemptByClassifiedInformation`; the old `exemptByNationalSecurity` (covering national security, confidentiality, _and_ individual privacy risk) was split so privacy risk became its own value, `exemptByPrivacyRisk`; `exemptByIPRestriction` was also added.

`organization`: removed the CMS-specific enum restriction (`Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services`) and generalized it to a free-text string with an example (`'18F'` or `'Navy'`) suitable for any agency.
Top-level `additionalProperties` changed from `false` to `true`, allowing agencies to extend the schema with their own custom fields.

`AIUseCaseID`, `SBOM`, and `feedbackMechanism` added to `required`; `categories`, `feedbackMechanisms`, `localisation`, `longDescription`, `platforms`, and `softwareType` removed from `required` (dropped entirely, see Removed above).
Field definitions are nested one level too deep under `properties.items` instead of directly under `properties` (the same structural bug present in the CMS schema's `schema-0.0.0.json`).

`permissions.usageType` is a single `string` value (not an array), so only one exemption reason could be declared per release, with a smaller 8-value exemption enum (`openSource`, `governmentWideReuse`, `exemptByLaw`, `exemptByNationalSecurity`, `exemptByAgencySystem`, `exemptByAgencyMission`, `exemptByCIO`, `exemptByPolicyDate`).
`organization` was restricted to a CMS-only enum value (`Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services`), despite this being the generic, agency-agnostic schema.
`identifier` field — a persistent unique ID used to track an asset across renames/migrations. Added to `properties` (right after `name`) and to `required`.
`downloads` property added to `reuseFrequency.properties`, alongside the existing `forks` and `clones`.
`permissions.usageType`
enum: M-16-21 exemptions are removed from the schema: `exemptByIPRestriction`, `exemptByAgencySystem`, `exemptByAgencyMission`, `exemptByCIO`, and `exemptByPolicyDate`

enum: `exemptByDisposableCode`, `exemptByExperimentalCode`, and `exemptByCommercialSoftware` are added, reflecting the SHARE IT Act's exclusions for exploratory/disposable code and commercial/COTS software.
Updated the `usageType` description text to define and renumber all 13 enum values to match.

Reworded the `reuseFrequency` description for clarity: _"Measures frequency of code reuse in various forms such as forks and clones for repositories, and downloads for packaged and distributed software."_

commits.message:
feat(pr-env): Cognito sign-in and a reaper exemption for demo environments (#620)

## Summary

Experiment for the NASA demo: a PR environment that people without CMS
accounts can sign in to. A PR labelled `pr-env:cognito` gets its own
Cognito user pool in place of dev's Okta client at its ALB rule, with
one test user per seeded role, so each person sees ZTMF as an owner,
ISSO, OpDiv admin, delegate, and so on. A PR labelled `pr-env:keep` gets
15 idle days before the reaper takes it instead of 7, so a demo
environment can sit untouched for two weeks. Without either label
nothing changes: PR environments stay on Okta and the reaper behaves as
before.

No application code changes. The API's existing header path already
verifies the ALB's ES256 `x-amzn-oidc-data` header and resolves the user
by email, which is how dev reads Okta today.

## Changes

* **`infrastructure/pr-env/cognito.tf` (new):** in cognito mode, a user
pool (self-signup off, username is the email, case-insensitive), a
hosted-UI domain with a random suffix, an ALB client returning to
`https://dev.ztmf.cms.gov/oauth2/idpresponse`, and one
`aws_cognito_user` per `cognito_users` entry with a permanent password
and no invitation email. The shared password comes from the
`PR_ENV_DEMO_PASSWORD` repo secret when it is set (else it is generated)
and is stored in the SSM SecureString
`/ztmf/pr/<repo>/<n>/cognito-password` either way. Also a separate
`ui-hs256-secret` parameter for the UI container.
* **`infrastructure/pr-env/variables.tf`:** `auth_provider` (`okta`
default, or `cognito`), `cognito_password` (sensitive; validated against
the pool's password policy), and `cognito_users` (default: one seeded
user per role: OWNER, HHS_READONLY_ADMIN, OPDIV_ADMIN,
OPDIV_READONLY_ADMIN, ISSO, SYSTEM_DELEGATE).
* **`infrastructure/pr-env/alb.tf`:** the listener rule's authenticate
action is `authenticate-oidc` (unchanged) or `authenticate-cognito`. The
Cognito session lasts the ALB maximum of 7 days under the cookie
`AWSELBAuthSessionCookie-pr-<repo>-<n>`, so it never clobbers dev's Okta
session on the same host.
* **`infrastructure/pr-env/ecs.tf`:** in cognito mode the API gets
`AUTH_HEADER_FIELD=x-amzn-oidc-data`, `AUTH_TOKEN_KEY_URL` (the same
regional ELB key endpoint dev uses), and `AUTH_OKTA_ISSUER` pinned to
the pool. The UI container signs its built-in `config.js` token with
`ui-hs256-secret`, which the API does not hold, because test mode still
accepts HS256 on the configured header. Okta mode is untouched.
* **`infrastructure/pr-env/iam.tf`:** the execution role can read the
UI's parameter when it exists.
* **`infrastructure/pr-env/outputs.tf`:** `auth_provider`,
`cognito_users`, `cognito_password_parameter`.
* **`.github/workflows/orchestration-pr.yml`:** passes
`auth_provider=cognito` when the PR carries `pr-env:cognito`, and
`PR_ENV_DEMO_PASSWORD` as `TF_VAR_cognito_password` only on those PRs.
Every other PR gets an empty value, because the variable is validated on
every apply and a secret that failed the password policy would otherwise
break Okta PRs too. The PR comment lists the test users and where the
password comes from. Teardown needs no change: destroy removes the
Cognito resources from state either way.
* **`scripts/pr-env-reaper.sh`:** an idle PR labelled `pr-env:keep` is
reaped after `KEEP_TTL_DAYS` (15) without a deploy instead of `TTL_DAYS`
(7), so the label stretches the limit rather than lifting it. The idle
comment on a reaped PR now names the date idleness was measured from and
the limit that applied. Each PR is read once per run instead of up to
three times. Closed PRs are still reaped, and a kept PR with no running
service is still reported.
* **`.github/workflows/pr-env-reaper.yml`:** `KEEP_TTL_DAYS: 15` next to
`TTL_DAYS`.
* **`infrastructure/pr-env/README.md`:** a Cognito section and the
reaper's 15-day keep limit.

## Deploy dependency

The reaper changes only take effect from main, because scheduled
workflows run from the default branch. Until this merges, `pr-env:keep`
does nothing and an idle environment is reaped at 7 days. Everything
else applies from this branch's own PR environment.

## Test plan

* `terraform fmt -check` and `terraform validate` in
`infrastructure/pr-env` pass. `bash -n scripts/pr-env-reaper.sh` passes,
and the workflows parse as YAML. The reaper was run with `--dry-run`
against stubbed `gh`, `aws` and `terraform`: closed, idle, kept under
the limit, kept past it, active, and never-deployed PRs each take the
expected path, and a kept PR with no running service is still reported.
* [x] Mark ready for review with `pr-env:cognito` and `pr-env:keep` on
the PR; the deploy job applies and the PR comment lists the six test
users.
* [ ] Open the environment URL in a private window: the Cognito hosted
sign-in appears, not CMS Okta.
* [ ] Sign in as `admiral.piett@executor.empire` with the
`PR_ENV_DEMO_PASSWORD` value: the app loads as Admiral Piett with ISSO
scope.
* [ ] In a second private window, sign in as
`grand.moff@deathstar.empire`: the app loads with OWNER access.
* [ ] A dev session in the same browser still works after signing in to

feat(misc#397): pin data calls to a questionnaire version and translate answers across versions (#630)

Closes CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#397 (epic ztmf-misc#307).

> [!NOTE]
> **Stacked on #625** (ztmf-misc#396), which is stacked on #623 and
#622. The base is #625's branch, so this diff is #397 only. Retarget to
`main` once #625 merges; CI's Backend job first runs then.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **API change for ztmf-misc#432:** data calls now carry
`questionnaire_versionid`. A `PUT /datacalls/{id}` ignores it; the pin
changes only through the new re-pin route.

## Summary

Every data call now names the questionnaire version it was answered
against, and answers can move between versions without losing meaning.
This is the last backend piece of the epic. Until a second version is
published, everything below behaves as today: every call is on v1, and
the rollover runs the same SQL plus an `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` that
fixes an older race (below).

## API

| Route | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `POST /datacalls` | Pins the newest published version, or the
`questionnaire_versionid` the body names. A draft, archived or missing
version is a 400 on `questionnaire_versionid`. The default is read under
the lifecycle lock (shared), so a publish or archive in flight cannot
change it between the read and the pin |
| `PUT /datacalls/{id}` | Unchanged; never moves the pin |
| `PUT /datacalls/{id}/questionnaire-version`
`{questionnaire_versionid}` | Re-pins an open call (below).
`CanWriteHHSWide` only. 200 returns the call plus `translated` and
`dropped` counts; 400 bad version; 403 past deadline or not authorized;
404 unknown call; 409 `VERSION_NOT_TRANSLATABLE` |

After merging #634, create writes `fiscal_year` and `cadence` with the
pin, inside the same transaction. PUT keeps #634's partial update and
still never moves the pin.

## How answers move between versions

One SQL fragment, `versionTranslationJoinSQL`, defines the translation.
It is shared by the rollover and by the re-pin's check and write, so
what the check approves is exactly what the write does. An answer
follows its function's `root_functionid` to the target version's
function, then to that function's option with the same score.

**Re-pin**, in one transaction:
1. lock the data call `FOR UPDATE`. Every score write holds it `FOR
SHARE` first (#623), so saves in flight finish and new ones wait. `FOR
UPDATE` rather than `NO KEY` also makes any insert that references the
call wait through its FK check, so a system marking the call complete
mid-re-pin is counted as touched;
2. return a no-op 200 if the version is unchanged (even when that
version has since been archived); lock the target `FOR SHARE` and
require it to be published (400 otherwise); then refuse past the
deadline (403), on the same boundary as score saves;
3. build the translation once into a transaction-scoped temp table
(`repin_map`); every later step reads it, so the call is locked for one
pass of the translation, not three;
4. preflight: among the answers with no row in the map, count those
someone touched (saved as done, any history, or on a system that marked
the call complete). If any, return 409 and change nothing. A structural
remap of given answers has no cheap inverse, so it waits for the next
call. Untouched answers elsewhere no longer block it;
5. otherwise update the pin first, append a `translate` revision to
every translated answer that has history, rewrite option ids, and delete
the rows with no row in the map (the untouched, carried-forward ones).
The check and the delete read the same map, so they cannot disagree
about which answers go. One `datacalls` event records from/to versions
and both counts.

`notes`, `status`, `last_updated_at` and every computed score are left
byte-identical; the integration test compares the aggregate and progress
responses before and after. The forked version mints new option ids, so
even a text-only re-pin rewrites every id. Undo then reports
`reasonIsTranslate` on those answers until their next edit; that cost
was accepted on the issue.

**Rollover.** Between calls on the same version, `copyPreviousScores`
runs the old SQL plus `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`; a golden-string unit
test pins it. The new call commits before the copy runs, so an answer
saved in between used to fail the whole copy with 23505 (older than this
PR); now it keeps its place and the rest is copied, still logged as an
under-copy. Across versions it dedups on `(fismasystemid,
root_functionid)` and joins the translation. The `ROLLOVER_ANOMALY`
comparison now uses the translatable count, and answers that
legitimately do not carry are logged as `VERSION_TRANSLATION_DROPPED
datacall=… from_version=… to_version=… dropped=…`. That token does not
match the CloudWatch filter.

## Where this departs from the issue text

- **Translation key.** The AC describes question lineage plus edition.
This uses function lineage plus score. #622's
`functions_root_version_uniq` makes a lineage at most one function per
version, so no answer fans out and no two land on one function. The
edition key cannot promise that for v1, which holds duplicate editions
(#622 deliberately did not add that constraint). For every version
published under #625's gate the two keys agree. Consequence: the AC's
"two editions onto one function" test cannot be built, because the case
cannot occur. **#625's body still describes #397 as keying on question
lineage and edition; it needs a one-line update.**
- **"Touched"** is done, *or* any revision, *or* a completed system, not
only done. An answer undone back to not-started was still touched by a
person, and dropping it would delete its history.
- **Log token** is uppercase `VERSION_TRANSLATION_DROPPED`, matching
`ROLLOVER_ANOMALY`.
- **Runbook.** ztmf has no runbook file, so the cascade note is under
Deploy notes.

## Decided: no re-pin after the deadline

A re-pin is refused for everyone after the deadline, although admins can
still save scores then, so a closed cycle keeps the version it was
answered against and its reported scores cannot shift. To correct a call
that was pinned wrongly (for example a backfill created without naming a
version): extend its deadline, re-pin, and restore the deadline. A
backfill can also name `questionnaire_versionid` at create.

## Tests

- Unit: golden same-version rollover SQL, the cross-version shape and
args, and that preflight, revisions and rewrite all read the one map
without translating again. `sanitizeErr` maps the new error to 409 +
code. `rbac_enforcement_test` covers the route.
- Integration (`versiontranslation_integration_test.go`):
- create pins the newest published version and refuses draft, archived
and missing versions; PUT cannot move the pin;
- re-pin: free swap with no answers; untouched answers remap and drop
with counts; given answers that translate move with history, identical
aggregate/progress, translate revisions on the target version, undo
refused, one audit event; untranslatable given answers and a completed
system are both 409 with nothing changed; same-version no-op survives
archiving; refusals (draft, 0, unknown call, past deadline, and a bad
version after the deadline is still a 400); given answers that translate
do not block dropping untouched ones;
- re-pin waits for an in-flight score write, and for a system marking
the call complete, which it then counts as touched (409). That test
fails if the re-pin's lock is `FOR NO KEY UPDATE`;
- rollover across versions: same version, removed option, removed
question (dropped and counted), added question;
- rollover keeps an answer saved into the new call before the copy, and
still copies the rest.
- Emberfall: 7 new cases (create/PUT pin behaviour, 400/403/404
refusals, a no-op re-pin). 327/327 locally, after merging #634 and #632.

## Deploy notes

- No migration.
- Deleting a data call cascades its scores and their `score_revisions`;
that was already true and is not changed here.
- Before a second version is published in production: ztmf-misc#432
shows the pin in the data-call UI, and backfill calls should name their
version.

feat(misc#396): fork, publish and archive questionnaire versions (#625)

Closes CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#396 (epic ztmf-misc#307).

> [!NOTE]
> **Stacked on #623** (ztmf-misc#395), which is stacked on #622
(ztmf-misc#394). The base is #623's branch, so this diff is #396 only.
Retarget to `main` once #623 merges; CI's Backend job first runs then.
Deploy after #623 has been live and verified.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Release note: from this PR all questionnaire content writes require
a draft version.** `POST/PUT /questions`, `/functions`,
`/functions/{id}/options` and `/functionoptions/{id}` against a
published version return **403 `VERSION_NOT_DRAFT`**. `POST
/questionnaire-versions` is how to get a draft. **Do not publish a
second version in production until #397 is deployed**, and not before
ztmf-insights filters catalog reads by version (gate on the issue).

## Summary

This is the lifecycle that gives a version meaning, plus the
content-write surface to author one: fork a draft, edit it, publish it
through a validation gate, and archive what is no longer current. It is
API-only. The content-write gaps #398 closed are assumed; this PR adds
what needs a version to be meaningful.

## API

| Route | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `GET /questionnaire-versions`, `GET /questionnaire-versions/{id}` |
List, newest first; one version |
| `POST /questionnaire-versions` `{label}` | Forks a draft from the
newest published version. A second draft is a 400 |
| `PUT /questionnaire-versions/{id}/publish`
`{dropped_root_functionids?}` | Runs the publish gate and the
dropped-lineage check, then publishes. 200 with the row, house style as
`/users/{id}/restore`. The body is needed only when the draft drops
lineages (below) |
| `PUT /questionnaire-versions/{id}/archive` | Archives a published
version that is no longer current. The current one is refused |
| `DELETE /questionnaire-versions/{id}` | Discards a draft and its
contents (not in the AC; without it a mistaken draft could never be
dropped, and it would block every later fork) |
| `DELETE /questions/{id}`, `/functions/{id}`, `/functionoptions/{id}` |
Draft only. A question takes its functions and their options with it;
published content is 403 |

Draft content is readable only by the same users: `GET /questions` and
`GET /functions` with a draft `versionid`, and `GET
/functions/{id}/options` for a draft function, return an empty list to
anyone else; `GET /questions/{id}` and `/functions/{id}` on draft rows
return 404. A content create naming a `versionid` that does not exist is
a 400 on `versionid`.

Every version and content write is behind the existing `CanWriteHHSWide`
gate, checked before the body is read or the database touched.
`rbac_enforcement_test` covers all of the new routes.

## How it works

- **Fork.** One transaction runs three `INSERT..SELECT`s mapped by
lineage (`root_questionid` / `root_functionid`), never by name. Forked
rows carry their source's root, not its id, and `ordr` is copied. The
legacy question-less band is skipped, since it could never publish. A
per-table count assertion rolls back a short copy.
- **Content writes** run through `catalogWrite` / `catalogDelete`:
  1. resolve the row's version;
2. lock it `FOR SHARE` as a draft, so a published target is 403 before
any content check;
  3. validate;
  4. write.

A new question with no `versionid` lands in the open draft. Function and
option versions come from their parent, via #622's triggers.
- **Lineage.** A create may name `root_questionid` / `root_functionid`
to restore a lineage a draft deleted. It must be a lineage root from an
earlier version and not already present. A function under a question and
edition that an earlier version already answers must restore that
lineage, not start a new one. An update cannot move a function to a
different question lineage or edition. Both rules come from one
`lineageRootsSQL`, shared by the write-time check and the gate. The
reason: #623's diff and #397's answer translation (#630) both key on
function lineage, so a question and edition must keep one lineage across
versions.
- **Publish gate.** Each failing rule is a 400 naming the offending rows
(capped at 20):
  - exactly four options scored 1–4 with no duplicates;
  - every function has a question;
  - every question has a function;
  - each function's pillar matches its question's;
  - one function per question and edition;
  - not an empty catalog (there is no unpublish);
  - no new lineage where one exists;
  - no lineage moved.
- **Dropped lineages.** After the gate, publish compares the draft's
function lineages with its parent's. If the draft leaves any out, it is
refused with a 400 on `dropped_root_functionids` listing each one
(`root_functionid`, the parent's question text, the environment).
Publishing again with exactly those ids confirms the drop; a missing or
extra id is refused again. This is the one way answers stop carrying
forward: a question deleted and re-created without its `root_questionid`
gets a fresh lineage, which the gate's lineage rules cannot see, and
only this check catches it. Restoring the lineage clears it from the
list. A dropped edition shows up the same way.
- **Concurrency.** Fork, publish, archive and discard serialize on a
transaction advisory lock, so a fork cannot copy a parent that a
concurrent publish is about to supersede. The lock order everywhere is:
lifecycle lock, then the version row, then content rows. Content writers
hold the version `FOR SHARE`, so publish, archive and discard wait for
in-flight writes and refuse later ones. Publish and archive take the row
`FOR NO KEY UPDATE`, which still excludes content writers but not the FK
checks every score save makes on a published version, so archiving a
version that calls are answering does not stall their saves. Discard
deletes the row, so it takes `FOR UPDATE` from the start.
- **Audit.** Lifecycle changes and catalog deletes write their event in
the same transaction. Deletes snapshot the row and every child row they
remove; a discard snapshots the whole draft. A question's pillar change
carries to its functions in the same transaction and records which ones
moved.
- **Migration 0072** indexes `scores(functionoptionid)`,
`score_revisions(functionid)` and `score_revisions(versionid)`. Deleting
draft options fires the NO ACTION checks from the first two, and
deleting the version row checks the third; without the indexes each
check was a sequential scan, and `score_revisions` grows with every
answer change. On production-like data, discarding a full fork took
about 25 s under the lifecycle lock; with the indexes it takes well
under a second, and the build takes about 50 ms. It is numbered 0072 to
sort after #634's 0070 and #622's 0071, whose
`score_revisions.versionid` it indexes.

## Draft-delete safety

A draft option can be deleted because no score can reference it. That
rests on two guards:
- #623's write check refuses a score option outside the call's pin;
- no data call can pin a draft. #630 (ztmf-misc#397) refuses a draft pin
at create and re-pin.

Published options are never deleted, which is also what keeps undo's
`prev_functionoptionid` resolvable (the item deferred from ztmf#596).

## Emberfall

The existing catalog cases are rewritten:
- **Baseline writes** now assert 403 `VERSION_NOT_DRAFT`. The message
names the remedy: the open draft's id when one exists, otherwise to fork
with `POST /questionnaire-versions` (covered in Go, since Emberfall
asserts the code only).
- **Validation and unusable-id cases** keep their 400s and 404s, since
validation runs before the draft check.

A new version flow at the end of the file covers:
- the list;
- `OPDIV_ADMIN` 403 on every version write, and on a content write while
a draft is open, so the 403 can only be the role gate;
- fork, then a second fork refused;
- a draft question created (with a body id, proving the route re-pin)
and edited;
- a missing pillar as a 400;
- the gate refusing to publish;
- draft delete, archive of the current version refused, discard.

Two things Emberfall cannot express:
- it templates URLs only, never bodies, and cannot index a list, so a
body cannot name a draft's runtime ids;
- the empire seed's catalog does not pass the publish gate.

So a successful publish, the edit-after-publish 403, archiving, the
per-rule gate tests and the draft re-pin cases are covered in Go
(`catalogversions_integration_test.go`,
`catalogrepin_integration_test.go`).

## Verification

- `make test-integration` passes on a fresh database against the
unmodified seed. `make test-e2e` passes all 320 Emberfall cases. `make
generate-openapi` is regenerated; Redocly reports the same 10 warnings
as `main`.
- **Go integration tests** cover:
- fork multisets per table (lineage, content, `ordr`) against the
parent, legacy band excluded;
  - each gate rule alone on an otherwise compliant draft;
- the full lifecycle (an archived version still resolves for a pinned
call);
  - lineage restore and the moved-lineage refusal;
  - pillar propagation;
  - delete and discard audit snapshots;
  - a published-root delete named in the 400;
  - duplicate historical lineages not blocking publish;
- dropped lineages: refused until named, a missing or extra id refused,
a question re-created without its root still listed and cleared once
restored, and a fork that drops nothing publishing without a body;
  - drafts readable by HHS-wide writers only, across the five reads.
- **Two review passes:**
- the first caught a fork/publish race, a deadlock between content
writes and discard, an empty-catalog publish, and lineage rules that
could make a draft unpublishable;
- the second caught further lock-order and race edges, plus the discard
audit gap.

  All fixed, each with a test.

feat(misc#395): resolve the pinned questionnaire version at every read site (#623)

Closes CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#395 (epic ztmf-misc#307).

> [!NOTE]
> **Stacked on #622** (ztmf-misc#394, migration 0071). The base is
#622's branch, so this diff excludes the schema. Retarget to `main` once
#622 merges; CI's Backend job first runs then. Deploy only after #622
has been live and verified, not in the same promotion.

## Summary

This makes the version pin from #622 select a catalog. A new helper in
`internal/model/questionnaireversion.go` limits every read that
enumerates applicable functions to the data call's pinned version. It
also adds the matching check to the score write path.

It **fails closed**, which is the opposite of the pillar scope: it is `=
(scalar subquery)`, so an unknown data call yields NULL and drops the
row. An empty questionnaire is loud; a doubled denominator is silent.
Pinning `functions.versionid` alone is enough, because 0071's composite
FKs keep a function's question and options in its version.

## Read sites

| Site | Change |
|---|---|
| `FindQuestionsByFismaSystem` | Pinned version with `datacallid`; the
newest published version without one |
| `FindAnswers` (export) | Inside the applicable branch and its "no
catalog" test, not the top-level `WHERE`, so a DECOMMISSIONED or
unmapped system keeps its history |
| `buildPillarScoresSQL` | Joined on each pair's own `dc` row, so a
closed cycle rescores against its own catalog. The stale "catalog drift
is not handled" comment is replaced |
| `buildScoreProgressSQL` | Rendered once into both `expected` and
`updated` (`strings.Count == 2`), so `lastupdatedat` is scoped too |
| `buildScoreDiffSQL` | Restricts each cycle to its own pinned version,
joins cycles on `root_functionid`, compares option **scores** across
versions (ids within one), and returns `root_functionid`, `pillarid` and
`pillar`. `functionid` is the To side's, matching the labels |
| `GET /functions`, `GET /questions` | Optional `versionid`; the newest
published version by default |

## Write path

`Score.Save`, `Score.Confirm` and `UndoScoreRevision` refuse an option
outside the data call's pinned version.
- **Why:** otherwise a draft or older version's option lands as a second
answer to the same question, under its own `functionid`. 0061's unique
index cannot see that clash, and the reads would hide the answer. It is
also what keeps draft options unanswerable, which #396's draft DELETE
relies on.
- **Placement:** on an update the version is checked before "different
question", so the error names the real reason.
- **Race with #397:** every score write locks the data call row `FOR
SHARE` before the score row: on create through the version check, and on
update, Confirm and undo before `lockScore`. So #397's re-pin, which
updates the data call row before any score, waits for in-flight writes
and cannot slip in between a check and its write. One lock order on
every path is also what keeps the two from deadlocking;
`TestScoreWritesLockTheDataCallFirstIntegration` pins it.

## Scoring change: system score averaged exactly

The system score used to be a `float8` `AVG` over pillar scores. That
sums in the order rows reach the window, which depends on the query
plan. Any query-shape change, including this PR's, shifted the last bit
of some system scores. On production-like data about one system score in
five moved by roughly 1e-16. **Every pillar score and every tier was
identical.**

It now averages the exact numeric pillar scores and converts once.
Pillar scores are unchanged byte for byte, and the system score no
longer depends on row order. This deploy carries a **one-time** last-bit
change to some system scores, so compare the aggregate on rounded scores
and tiers for this one promotion. From here on, aggregates stay
byte-identical across query changes.

## Not changed, on purpose

- **A PUT that keeps an out-of-version option.** Save checks the version
only when the option changes, so the questionnaire's Next-click PUT does
no extra query. It does now take the data call's share lock (see the
race note above); share locks don't block each other, so it waits only
on a data call update. Such a stored row cannot arise through the API,
and `questionnaire_version_anomalies()` reports it if anything writes
one.
- **`GET /questions` now rejects unknown query parameters (400).** That
is how the other list endpoints already behave.
- **No `versionid` on the `Function` / `Question` JSON or write
structs.** Content writes belong to #396.
- **Cross-version "changed" compares option scores.** Switching between
two options with the same score, or renaming an option, does not show as
a change between cycles on different versions: options have no lineage
column, so the score is the best identity available. Within one version
option ids are compared, as before.
- **Diff labels come from the To side.** When the two cycles pin
different versions, a row's function, question and pillar read as the
cycle under review words them.

## Frontend counterpart

CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-ui#761 (ztmf-misc#432) passes `datacallid` in
`useQuestionBreakdown`, groups `ScoreDiffModal` by the `pillar` on each
diff row instead of fetching questions, and adds `root_functionid`,
`pillarid` and `pillar` to `ScoreDiff` in `src/types.ts`. It must deploy
after this PR, and before a second version is published.

## Verification

- **Suites:** `make test-integration` passes on a fresh database against
the unmodified seed. `make test-e2e` runs 309 Emberfall cases with 0
failures. `make generate-openapi` is regenerated; Redocly reports the
same 10 warnings as `main`.
- **Unit tests** pin:
  - the fragment text;
  - the fail-closed shape;
  - the two progress CTEs;
  - the pillar-scores join;
- the diff's lineage join and score comparison, and each cycle's version
filter on its own datacallid placeholder (including under the user
scope);
  - the exact system-score average.
- **CI regression bar**
(`TestQuestionnaireVersionRegressionBarIntegration`): fork an identical
version, publish it, pin a twin of data calls 103 and 104 to it.
Aggregate, progress, export and diff must match, and the original calls
must not move, including an unmapped system's export rows. An
out-of-version answer must contribute no count, no `lastupdatedat` and
no diff row, and a real change must surface with its lineage and the To
side's `functionid`.
- **Write path:** draft and other-version options are refused on create,
beside an existing answer, on update, on confirm and on undo.
- **Mutation-checked:** removing each predicate or guard in turn fails a
test.
- **Production-like data,** on a throwaway copy:
- every read matched #622 byte for byte, apart from the one-time
system-score bits above;
- after forking and publishing an identical v2, every pinned read was
byte-identical;
- a v2 twin of the busiest cycle matched its source exactly (scores,
progress, export, questionnaire), with an empty diff.

**Still needed on a production restore** (from the issue's ACs): the
fork-publish-pin comparison across a real cycle.

feat(misc#394): add questionnaire_versions and pin the catalog to a baseline (#622)

Closes CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#394 (epic ztmf-misc#307).

## Summary

The schema half of questionnaire versioning, deployed as a no-op.
Migration 0071 adds `questionnaire_versions` with one published baseline
(version 1) and puts every existing question, function, option and data
call on it. Every join it adds is an identity join, and nothing reads
`versionid` until ztmf-misc#395. No Go code outside `migrations/`
changes.

## What 0071 adds

| Change | Why |
|---|---|
| `questionnaire_versions` (`draft`/`published`/`archived`), baseline
row 1, partial unique index allowing one draft | The version entity;
#396 forks against the one-draft index |
| `versionid INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1` on `questions`, `functions`,
`functionoptions`; `questionnaire_versionid` on `datacalls` | Appended
last with a default, so the seed's positional inserts and every existing
writer keep working |
| `root_questionid` / `root_functionid`, defaulted to the row's own id
by a `BEFORE INSERT` trigger | Lineage is the cross-version identity;
nothing correlates by name (the 0045 defect). The trigger defaults and
never rejects |
| `UNIQUE (root, versionid)`, and a composite self-FK requiring a root
to be its own root | One row per lineage per version, so #397's
translation cannot fan out; a fork that copies a forked id instead of
its root fails |
| Composite FKs `functions(questionid, versionid) → questions` and
`functionoptions(functionid, versionid) → functions` | A row cannot
point across a version boundary. `functions.questionid` is nullable for
the legacy band, and `MATCH SIMPLE` skips those rows |
| `score_revisions.versionid` / `root_functionid`, backfilled, then set
by a trigger from `functions` | Stored at write time because deriving
through `datacalls` breaks once #397 re-pins an open cycle. A trigger
rather than a `DEFAULT`, since `insertScoreRevision` does not name the
columns and a default would record the baseline forever |
| New `functions` / `functionoptions` rows take their parent's
`versionid` (`BEFORE INSERT` trigger) | `Function.Save` and
`FunctionOption.Save` do not name `versionid`, so under a draft parent a
`DEFAULT 1` would land the row in the baseline and fail the composite
FK. A missing parent keeps the row's own value so the FK still reports
23503. `questions` has no parent, so #396's question writer must set
`versionid` itself |
| `questionnaire_version_anomalies()`, logged by the migration as
`QUESTIONNAIRE_VERSION_ANOMALY` (`RAISE WARNING`) | Catches the failure
this epic fears most: a data call pinned to a version its scores do not
reference, which reads as "Not Assessed" with nothing erroring. Also
counts duplicate editions as a non-fatal probe |
| `make check-questionnaire-versions` and
`backend/docs/check-questionnaire-versions.sql` | Runs the orphan
pre-checks before deploy and the anomaly checks after it |

## Decisions

- **Numbered 0071.** tern versions migrations by position, not by file
name. #634's `0070datacallsfiscalyear.go` merged first and is recorded
as version 68 on deployed databases, so this file has to sort after it:
a database at 68 runs it as 69. Under its old name, 0068, a database at
68 would have treated it as applied and skipped it. A database that ran
this stack before the rename (a local copy or a PR environment) recorded
the old files as 68 and 69; rebuild it.

- **`UNIQUE (questionid, datacenterenvironment, versionid)` is not
added.** The data checked here is clean, but production has never been
probed. A failing unique index would abort the migration, and the API
would not start. #396's publish gate enforces the rule for every new
version. The baseline never passes that gate, so #397's translation join
must keep its `DISTINCT ON`, and the `duplicate_editions` check reports
any duplicates in the deploy log.
- **Orphaned catalog rows fail readably.** Rows written under
`session_replication_role = replica` can dangle despite the existing FKs
(see 0060). The migration raises `ZTMF394_ORPHANED_CATALOG` with counts
instead of a bare 23503 or 23502.
- **Locks are taken up front, in the order a score save takes them**:
`functionoptions`, `score_revisions`, `datacalls`, `functions`,
`questions`. A save in flight on an old task during the rolling deploy
waits instead of deadlocking.
- **The down migration refuses** (`ZTMF394_VERSIONS_EXIST`) once any
version other than the baseline exists, because dropping `versionid`
would merge two catalogs with nothing to tell them apart.
- The single-column FKs stay. They are now redundant with the composite
ones, but harmless, and #396/#397 can drop them.

## Rollback

As with every migration here, a pre-0071 image refuses to start against
a database that has run 0071 (`MIGRATION_VERSION_MISMATCH`). Rolling
back the image therefore also needs `dbversions` set back by one (to 68,
#634's 0070). The 0071 schema can stay in place: every new column has a
default and no old code reads it.

## Deploy

`ztmf` only, no frontend coupling.

- [ ] **Snowflake first.** `questions`, `functions`, `functionoptions`
and `datacalls` are in the ztmf-insights data-sync allowlist, which
exports `SELECT *`. The Snowflake tables need the new columns before
this deploys. Separately, before #396 creates a second version,
ztmf-insights queries that enumerate functions need a version filter.
- [ ] **Deploy outside the ztmf-insights sync window.** 0071 takes
`ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` locks on five tables with a 10 s `lock_timeout`; a
long sync read on any of them makes the migration time out and the new
task fail to start.
- [ ] Before deploying to each environment, run `make
check-questionnaire-versions` against it. It must report no orphans.
- [ ] Capture
`/scores/aggregate?datacallid=<current>&include_pillars=true` before,
and confirm it is byte-identical after.
- [ ] After deploy, confirm the logs carry no
`QUESTIONNAIRE_VERSION_ANOMALY` token and that `make
check-questionnaire-versions` is clean. Let it sit on dev for a day
before #395.

## Verification

- `make test-integration` passes on a fresh database against an
unmodified `_test_data_empire.sql`. `make test-e2e` runs 309 Emberfall
cases with 0 failures, with the existing aggregate assertions
unmodified.
- `0071questionnaireversions_integration_test.go` covers:
  - the seed landing on the baseline;
- lineage defaults and explicit roots, plus rejection of a non-root or
missing root;
- all three cross-version writes rejected, each asserting the constraint
that fired;
  - revisions taking their function's version and lineage root;
  - every anomaly check firing;
  - the one-draft index;
  - the down migration's refusal;
  - the readable orphan failure for all three kinds of dangling row;
  - a down-then-up round trip over the seeded rows.
- **On production-like data** (several hundred thousand answers across
several data calls), the migration applied in well under a second with
every anomaly count at zero. The aggregate, progress, export, score-diff
and questionnaire outputs for every data call were byte-identical before
and after.

**Still needed on a production restore** (from the issue's ACs, not
runnable here): the uniqueness probe, and the before/after aggregate
comparison across a real cycle.

we can demo the app and work in it day to day without real federal data.

decommissioned system and a reactivated one, delegates (one of them
expired), an answer with undo history, two data center mismatches, and
an open FY2027 call that is part-way through. The other OpDivs get the
rest of the portfolio (23 new systems and 38 new users in total), so
OWNER and HHS-level views aren't empty either.

up, and data call 7. Existing fixture rows keep their ids, roles and

- **Reload safety.** Re-running the file on a persistent volume used to
duplicate events and flip open answers to done, because the older bulk
audit blocks had no upper bound. Those blocks are now bounded and
guarded. Three loads in a row produce identical row counts.

long-lived local volume, call 5 closes about 200 days after the volume
was seeded. Recreate the volume to reset it.

feat(ztmf#631): store the fiscal year and cadence on data calls (#634)

Closes CMS-Enterprise/ztmf#631

Part of
[ztmf-misc#440](https://github.com/CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc/issues/440).

A data call's fiscal year and cadence only lived in its name, and the UI
parsed them out. This stores both as columns so the name can be a
free-text title.

## Before this deploys

- [x] Add `FISCAL_YEAR` and `CADENCE` to
`BUS_ZEROTRUST.CORE.ZTMF_DATACALLS`. The data-sync Lambda `SELECT *`s
`datacalls`, so without them that table's sync fails on the next run.
Steps are in the ztmf-insights `docs/pipelines/data-sync.md` runbook
("When a ztmf migration touches a synced table").
- [ ] Confirm every data call name in dev, impl and prod starts with
`FY##` or `FY####`. The migration stops and lists any row that doesn't,
by design.
- [ ] Deploy
[ui!766](https://github.com/CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-ui/pull/766) right after
this. Until it lands, the create form on main does not send
`fiscal_year`, so creating a data call returns a 400. Reading data calls
is unaffected.

## What changed

- New columns on `datacalls`: `fiscal_year` (integer, not null, 2000 to
2999) and `cadence` (`annual` or `quarterly`, defaults to `annual`).
Both are CHECK constraints, the same style as 0046 and 0048.
- The migration backfills every existing row from its name. An `FY##` or
`FY####` prefix gives the year (`FY26` is 2026). A call is quarterly
when `Q1` to `Q4` comes right after the year, with or without a space
(`FY26 Q2`, `FY26Q2`), which matches the UI rule in
[ui!765](https://github.com/CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-ui/pull/765). A quarter
later in the name, like `FY2027 Zero Trust Q2 Review`, is annual.
Anything else is annual. If a name has no usable year, the migration
fails and lists each row by id and name. It does not guess. Down drops
both columns.
- Every data call response now carries `fiscal_year` and `cadence`.
- Create requires `datacall`, `deadline` and `fiscal_year`. `cadence`
defaults to `annual`. Update is partial: any field left out keeps its
stored value, so `PUT {"cadence":"quarterly"}` changes only the cadence.
Bad values are a 400 that names the field.
- `SaveDataCall` reads the path id with `pathInt32`, like the other
handlers. `/datacalls/0` is a 404 and `/datacalls/0012` is call 12. A
`datacallid` in a POST body no longer turns the create into an update.
- Titles are unique ignoring case (unique index on `lower(datacall)`),
because the UI resolves deep links by title case-insensitively. If
existing titles already differ only by case, the migration fails and
lists them. A case-only duplicate on create or update is a 400, the same
as an exact duplicate.
- The name has no shape check anywhere in the backend. Latest and
current data call still resolve by deadline.
- `openapi.yaml` is regenerated.

## Migration number

The file is 0070, but tern records a migration by its position in the
list, so a database records this one as version 68. Calvin's
questionnaire version stack
([ztmf!622](https://github.com/CMS-Enterprise/ztmf/pull/622),
[ztmf!623](https://github.com/CMS-Enterprise/ztmf/pull/623),
[ztmf!625](https://github.com/CMS-Enterprise/ztmf/pull/625),
[ztmf!630](https://github.com/CMS-Enterprise/ztmf/pull/630)) uses the
0068 and 0069 file names. Whichever of the two lands second has to
rename its files to sort after the other's. If it doesn't, a database
that already ran the first would record the wrong migration under each
version and skip one.

## Overlap with ztmf!632

[ztmf!632](https://github.com/CMS-Enterprise/ztmf/pull/632) rewrites
`_test_data_empire.sql` and `emberfall_tests.yml`. I kept my seed change
to adding a `fiscal_year` value to each existing data call insert.
Whichever of us merges second will need to add `fiscal_year` to any data
call rows the other adds. Its call 5 rename to "FY2027 Imperial Zero
Trust Data Call" would take `fiscal_year` 2027.

A local dev volume seeded from the current empire data has call 5 named
"Audit Fields Smoke Cycle". It has no FY prefix, so this migration will
stop on it. Rename it or rebuild the volume.

## Testing

- `make test-unit`: pass
- `make test-integration`: pass. The new 0070 test runs down, loads
names, and runs up again. It covers two and four digit years, quarterly
names, a descriptive title, a retry, the CHECKs, and a set of names that
fail with every bad row listed.
- `make test-e2e`: pass, 301 ran, 0 failed. New cases cover the
defaulted cadence, partial updates that send one field, case-only
duplicate titles, the path id, and the 400s.
- `redocly lint`: valid, same 10 warnings as main.

fix(api): fail closed on an empty self-scope in /scores/aggregate (#628)

Closes CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#427

`GET /scores/aggregate` now returns an empty list to an ISSO, ISSM or
system delegate who has no assigned systems. Before, that caller got
every system's aggregate, and could pick any single system with
`?fismasystemid`.

| Caller | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Self-scoped, no assigned systems | every system | `[]` |
| Self-scoped, no assigned systems, `?fismasystemid=N` | system N | `[]`
|
| Self-scoped with assignments | their systems | unchanged |
| Admin and OpDiv tiers | unchanged | unchanged |

### Why it happened

This endpoint self-scopes by the caller's assigned-system ID list
instead of the `UserID` join the other score reads use. The SQL builder
only added the system filter when that list was non-empty, so an empty
list meant no filter. `FindScoresAggregate` also copied `?fismasystemid`
into the empty list, which is how a single system could be selected.

### Fix

A `SystemScope` type next to `OpDivScope` carries the list plus a
server-owned `RestrictToFismaSystemIDs` flag (`schema:"-"`, so the query
string can never set it). A restricted, empty list emits `FALSE`, the
same fail-closed rule `OpDivWhere` already applies to OpDiv tiers. The
controller sets it through `scopeScoresAggregateInput`, and the
`?fismasystemid` copy is gone; the builder already filters on
`fs.fismasystemid = $n` on its own, so admin results are identical.

I kept the ID list rather than switching this endpoint to the `UserID`
join, so assigned callers get exactly the same SQL and query plan as
today. The judgment call worth a look is `FindScores` also applying
`SystemWhere`: nothing sets it there yet, but leaving it out would make
a future caller silently unfiltered.

The other score reads (`/scores`, `/scores/progress`, `/scores/diff`,
the export) already scope by `UserID` and return nothing for this user.
They are unchanged.

### Testing

- Unit tests for `SystemScope` and the builder: restricted-empty emits
`FALSE` with and without `fismasystemid`, an assigned list emits the
`IN` list, admin and OpDiv tiers add nothing new. The role matrix for
`scopeScoresAggregateInput` is covered, and decoding
`RestrictToFismaSystemIDs` from the query is a 400.
- Integration tests with zero-assignment ISSO, ISSM and delegate users
on `/scores/aggregate`, `/scores` and `/scores/progress`, plus an
assigned ISSO who sees only their own systems. With the controller
change reverted, all five aggregate requests fail.
- An integration test that `FindScores` honors a restricted
`SystemScope` (nil, empty, empty plus `fismasystemid`, and a one-system
list).
- One seed user with no assignments in `_test_data_empire.sql` and 4
Emberfall cases. The two aggregate cases fail on main; the `/scores` and
`/scores/progress` cases already passed and keep those endpoints in
step.
- `make test-unit`, `make test-integration` and `make test-full` pass.
No schema change, so `_test_data.sql` is untouched, and `make
generate-openapi` shows no drift.

feat(misc#434): constrain answer option scores to 1-4; tighten scoring tests (#624)

Part of CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#434. Cleanup from Calvin's review of
#621, plus a DB check that answer option scores stay 1-4.

**Migration 0067** adds `functionoptions_score_check CHECK (score
BETWEEN 1 AND 4)`. `FunctionOption.validate` already rejects anything
else with a 400, so this only stops a write that bypasses the API, such
as a hand-run load, from scoring below the 1.25 floor. It is guarded so
a rerun is a no-op, takes a 10s `lock_timeout` like 0061/0065, and the
down drops it. The table is about 2k rows, so a plain validating `ADD
CONSTRAINT` is fine. Local data is 1,728 options, all 1-4.

**Judgment call:** this and Calvin's #622 both number their migration
`0067`. Tern tracks a position, not names, so whichever merges second
must be renumbered `0068` or one migration is silently skipped. This one
is small and should go first; I asked on #622.

**Test fixes (no behavior change):**
- The reduced-scope integration test now proves Not Assessed by answer
count (nothing in-scope answered) rather than by the 1.25 score, which
an all-1s system also produces.
- The HHS formula fixture uses `reducedPillarScopeSQL` instead of a
hand-written scope check, so it can't drift from the aggregate.
- `purgeIntegrationTestRows` removes the "ztmf-misc#433 fixture"
question and function, so a killed run doesn't leave a stray question
behind.
- The spreadsheet test uses an answered score of 1 instead of 0.
- An emberfall comment that said there is no CHECK on this column now
says validate returns the 400 before the CHECK is reached.

**Testing:** `make test-unit`, `make test-integration` (104 passed,
including a new migration test that proves 0, 5 and -1 are rejected, a
rerun is a no-op and down drops the check) and `make test-full`
(emberfall 280/280) pass. No API, OpenAPI or emberfall assertion change.

**Deploy:** the migration runs at API startup on merge, DEV then PROD.
Prod option scores were checked earlier as 1-4 only. If a bad row
existed, startup would fail loudly at version 66 with nothing changed.

feat(misc#432): show the questionnaire version a new data call pins (#761)

* fix(misc#392): keep undo focus and history scoped to the undone question

Move focus to View history, or the drawer panel, after any undo outcome
that can unmount the Undo button. Pin the undone scoreid so a mid-request
navigation refreshes the right history, and skip draft and focus steps
once the user has moved on. Name the drawer's scroll region separately.

* fix(misc#392): scope a failed undo to the undone question

A refused, conflicting or past-deadline undo now invalidates the undone row's
history (pinned at mutate time) instead of refetching whichever question is on
screen, and skips its warning once the user has moved on. Focus after an undo
reads the drawer from the DOM, and the moved-on context is set after commit
rather than during render.

* feat(misc#432): show the questionnaire version a new data call pins

DataCallModal names the newest published version the API will pin, and warns
when the call it carries answers from used a different one. The question
breakdown reads the cycle's own version, and the score diff groups by the
pillar each row carries, so older cycles still line up once a second version
is published.

* fix(misc#432): scope undo cleanup to its cycle and row; toast unplaced create errors

The undo's moved-on check now includes the data call, and a refused undo
reloads scores only while the same system and call are on screen. The undone
row travels with the request, so a paused undo still targets it. Focus after an
undo follows the drawer's open state, including after a generic failure. A 400
on a field the create form has no input for is toasted. docs/ScoreDiffModal.md

feat(ui#762): read the stored fiscal year and cadence; free-text data call titles (#766)

* feat(ui#762): read the stored fiscal year and cadence; free-text data call titles

Group the data call picker by the stored fiscal_year and trend by the
stored cadence. Nothing reads a year or cadence out of a call's title
any more, and no agency name is attached to a call in the picker, the
system table call menu, the dashboards or the trend.

An OpDiv follows the quarterly trend series when any of its systems was
scored in the newest quarterly call; the aggregate and every other
OpDiv follow the annual series. On prod data this picks the same series
the CMS-coded rule did.

The create form takes a free-text title, a fiscal year, a cadence
(annual by default) and a deadline.

* fix(ui#762): keep every later fiscal year's annual call in the quarterly trend

The quarterly series took only the newest annual call, so once an FY27
call exists FY26 ZTM would drop out of the CMS trend and FY27's prior
call would become the last quarterly call. The series is now every
quarterly call, plus every annual call from a fiscal year later than
the last quarterly call's, plus the newest annual call. An annual call
from the last quarterly call's own fiscal year (FY25 ZTM next to FY2025
Q3) stays out, so prod's CMS line does not change.

The regression fixture now uses prod's data calls and deadlines from
the FY2026 rollover fix, with expectations computed from main's
name-parsing code.

* fix(#764): compute the FIPS baseline from the system record so it shows for every OpDiv

The baseline read fips_impact_level/fips_ceiling off the Insights payload,
